title: Winter sun from Gatwick in January: direct flights compared
author: Matt
intro: In January, Gatwick has direct flights to the Canaries, Madeira, Morocco, Egypt, Cape Verde, Dubai and the Caribbean, from about 3½ to 9 hours away. Here's how they compare for warmth, flight time and time difference, and what's new this winter.
seo_title: Winter sun from Gatwick in January: 3½ to 9 hrs away
seo_description: The Canaries are about 4 hours from Gatwick and 20-22°C in January. Egypt, Dubai and Cape Verde are warmer, and the Caribbean is 28-29°C. Compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warm and close:** the Canaries, 4¼ hrs
- **Warmest:** the Caribbean, 28-29°C
- **New this winter:** Jet2 from Gatwick
- **No time difference:** Canaries, Madeira

The temperatures here are average daytime highs for January, from the climate figures in our guides. Flight times are typical direct times from Gatwick. We checked routes in November 2026 from airline announcements, but timetables change, so check the airline's own schedule for your dates before you book.

Gatwick has more winter sun choice than any other UK airport we've covered, so the real question is how far you want to fly.

sections.heading: What's new from Gatwick this winter
sections.text:
- **Jet2** is flying from Gatwick for the first time this winter, with winter sun routes including the Canaries, and new routes to [Agadir](/destinations/agadir), [Hurghada](/destinations/hurghada) and [Sharm el-Sheikh](/destinations/sharm-el-sheikh).
- **British Airways** has added a daily Gatwick flight to [Barbados](/destinations/barbados) from 25 October 2026, alongside its Heathrow service, and extended its daily [Antigua](/destinations/antigua) flights to the end of April 2027.
- **easyJet**, the biggest airline at Gatwick, flies to the Canaries, Madeira, Morocco and Egypt in winter.

With Jet2 now competing with easyJet and BA on many of the same routes, it's worth comparing all three for the same dates.

sections.heading: The Canaries and Madeira: short and easy
sections.text:
For a week of winter sun without jet lag, the Canaries are the obvious choice: about four hours away, on UK time, and around 20 to 22°C in January. [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) and [Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria) are the warmest, [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote) is calmer, and [Fuerteventura](/destinations/fuerteventura) has the biggest beaches.

[Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is a little cooler at about 19°C but greener, with levada walks and gardens. Our [Madeira or Tenerife](/blog/madeira-or-tenerife) post compares the two.

Tip: in the Canaries and Madeira, the sun sets around 6pm UK time in January, about two hours later than in London, so the days feel much longer.

sections.heading: Egypt, Cape Verde and Dubai: properly warm
sections.text:
- **Egypt's Red Sea:** [Hurghada](/destinations/hurghada) and [Sharm el-Sheikh](/destinations/sharm-el-sheikh) are about 21 to 22°C, with sunshine nearly every day and coral reefs offshore. You'll need a visa, usually bought on arrival.
- **[Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde):** about 25°C, with long white beaches, but often windy.
- **[Dubai](/destinations/dubai):** about 24°C, with Emirates flying from Gatwick several times a day. It's four hours ahead, so allow a day to adjust on a short trip.

If you want warm sea as well as warm air, January is a bit early for the Red Sea, where the water is cooler than in spring. Cape Verde and the Caribbean have warmer seas.

sections.heading: The Caribbean: the big trip
sections.text:
January is peak season in the Caribbean, with dry, sunny days of about 28 to 29°C. From Gatwick, British Airways flies direct to [Barbados](/destinations/barbados) and [Antigua](/destinations/antigua), both about 8½ to 9 hours away and four hours behind the UK.

It's the most expensive option here, and a long way for under a week, but it's the only one that guarantees beach-hot weather and a warm sea. [St Lucia](/destinations/st-lucia) is another option, so check which Caribbean routes fly on your dates.

Watch out: the first week of January is still part of the Christmas holidays, so prices stay high until the schools go back. From the second week they usually drop.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Gatwick?
sections.text:
Start with [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) for an easy week, [Sharm el-Sheikh](/destinations/sharm-el-sheikh) for guaranteed warmth, or [Barbados](/destinations/barbados) if you want the full Caribbean. The [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) page has more ideas, and our guide to [how early to arrive at Gatwick](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-gatwick-airport) covers the airport itself.

Can't agree on how far to go? Read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or add your shortlist to somewhere.party and let the draw choose.

faqs.question: Where is hot in January from Gatwick?
faqs.answer: The Canaries are about 20 to 22°C and four hours away. Egypt, Cape Verde and Dubai are 21 to 25°C, and Barbados and Antigua are 28 to 29°C.

faqs.question: Does Jet2 fly from Gatwick?
faqs.answer: Yes. Jet2 started flying from Gatwick for winter 2026/27, with winter sun routes including the Canaries, Agadir, Hurghada and Sharm el-Sheikh.

faqs.question: Can you fly direct from Gatwick to Barbados?
faqs.answer: Yes. British Airways flies daily from Gatwick to Barbados from 25 October 2026, as well as from Heathrow. The flight is about 8½ to 9 hours.

faqs.question: What is the closest winter sun to Gatwick?
faqs.answer: Marrakech and Madeira are about 3½ to 4 hours away, but at 18 to 19°C they're mild rather than hot. The Canaries, at about 4 hours, are a little warmer.
